translate_en|mods/UH60BlackHawk/42/media: Keys for flying the AH-64. W / S / A / D (forward, back, turn) and F (searchlight) are the game's own vehicle keys.
AH-64 sound volume (also follows the game's Sound and Vehicle engine volume)
The EC135's sound. It also follows the game's own Sound and Vehicle engine volume.
The MH-6 Little Bird's sound. It also follows the game's own Sound and Vehicle engine volume.
Keys for flying the OH-58D. W / S / A / D (forward, back, turn) and F (searchlight) are the game's own vehicle keys.
OH-58D sound volume (also follows the game's Sound and Vehicle engine volume)
The UH-60 Black Hawk's sound. It also follows the game's own Sound and Vehicle engine volume.
How long the engine keeps running with nobody in the pilot's seat before it switches itself off. 0 switches it off straight away. -1 never switches it off. Default 60.
How much ammunition a AH-64 Apache the world spawns has loaded. Game default: 8 HE rockets and 4 fire rockets (its gun belt is the player's own and is not set here). Half = 4 + 4, Full = 8 + 8.
How charged the battery of a AH-64 Apache the world spawns is.
The condition of every part of a AH-64 Apache the world spawns. Game default keeps the game's own (its Car Condition setting and the place it is in).
Whether a AH-64 Apache the world spawns has its doors locked.
How much fuel a AH-64 Apache the world spawns has in its tank.

Where the key of a AH-64 Apache the world spawns is. Game default: the key is put in the ignition for you when you climb in (single player), so a found aircraft can always be started. No key anywhere: it has to be hotwired (if allowed below) or an admin hands the key out. In the vehicle: in its glove box or storage. On the ground beside it: a few steps away.
Empty: a AH-64 Apache the world spawns has nothing in its glove box, seats or storage.
Off: only its key starts a AH-64 Apache - nobody can hotwire it, whatever their skills. For roleplay servers that hand vehicles out with their keys.

A rocket burst brings down the walls, windows, doors, furniture, fences and trees around it, and a FIRE rocket sets it alight. Off: rockets only hurt zombies. On a server a safehouse is never touched.

Airport service areas (the airfields of the game's map and of map mods). Spawn settings are read when the game starts and only change areas nobody has explored yet - restart the game (or server) after changing them.

Military vehicle zones - the game's own map has none; map mods with bases add them. Spawn settings are read when the game starts and only change areas nobody has explored yet - restart the game (or server) after changing them.

0 = from the start. Before this in-game day, an ordinary vehicle of that place spawns instead - for example military hardware only after the collapse. Only areas first explored before that day are affected.
Writes every AH-64 Apache the world spawns - and every one turned away by the limit or the first day - to the console (the server's console.txt) with where it is.

0 = no limit. Once the world has spawned this many AH-64 Apaches, it puts an ordinary vehicle of that place there instead (the game's own way of keeping a unique vehicle unique). Vehicles an admin or a debug menu spawns never count and are never stopped. Counted per world.

How often the world spawns the AH-64 Apache at airports and military bases. Default is how rare it has always been; Off means the world never spawns one (admins and debug menus still can). Ultra rare x0.05, Very rare x0.2, Rare x0.5, Common x2.5, Very common x5, Abundant x15. Spawn settings are read when the game starts and only change areas nobody has explored yet - restart the game (or server) after changing them.
